name: Acadia
about: Rocky Atlantic coastline and granite peaks on Mount Desert Island, including Cadillac Mountain.

name: American Samoa
about: Rainforest, coral reefs and beaches in the South Pacific; the only US national park south of the equator.

name: Arches
about: More than 2,000 natural stone arches, including Delicate Arch.

name: Badlands
about: Eroded buttes and pinnacles beside a wide mixed-grass prairie, rich in fossils.

name: Big Bend
about: Desert, mountains and the canyons of the Rio Grande on the border with Mexico.

name: Biscayne
about: Mostly underwater: coral reefs, keys and mangroves, best seen by boat or snorkel.

name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison
about: A deep, narrow, sheer-walled canyon carved by the Gunnison River.

name: Bryce Canyon
about: Amphitheatres filled with hoodoos, the tall rock spires the park is famous for.

name: Canyonlands
about: Canyons, mesas and buttes carved by the Colorado and Green rivers.

name: Capitol Reef
about: The Waterpocket Fold, a nearly 100-mile wrinkle in the Earth’s crust, and the orchards of Fruita.

name: Carlsbad Caverns
about: More than 119 caves, including the vast Big Room, and summer evening bat flights.

name: Channel Islands
about: Five islands off the California coast, known for sea caves, kelp forests and the island fox.

name: Congaree
about: Old-growth bottomland forest with some of the tallest trees in eastern North America.

name: Crater Lake
about: The deepest lake in the United States, filling the caldera of a collapsed volcano.

name: Cuyahoga Valley
about: Forests, waterfalls and a scenic railroad along the Cuyahoga River between Cleveland and Akron.

name: Death Valley
about: The hottest, driest and lowest national park, with Badwater Basin 282 feet below sea level.

name: Denali
about: Six million acres of wilderness around Denali, the highest peak in North America.

name: Dry Tortugas
about: Seven small islands about 70 miles west of Key West, with the 19th-century Fort Jefferson.

name: Everglades
about: The largest subtropical wilderness in the US, home to alligators, manatees and wading birds.

name: Gates of the Arctic
about: Roadless wilderness north of the Arctic Circle in the Brooks Range.

name: Gateway Arch
about: The 630-foot stainless-steel arch on the St. Louis riverfront.

name: Glacier
about: Glacier-carved peaks and valleys crossed by the Going-to-the-Sun Road.

name: Glacier Bay
about: Tidewater glaciers, fjords and whales in southeast Alaska.

name: Grand Canyon
about: A mile-deep canyon carved by the Colorado River.

name: Grand Teton
about: The jagged Teton Range rising above Jackson Hole and its lakes.

name: Great Basin
about: Lehman Caves, ancient bristlecone pines and Wheeler Peak in eastern Nevada.

name: Great Sand Dunes
about: The tallest sand dunes in North America, below the Sangre de Cristo Mountains.

name: Great Smoky Mountains
about: Forested mountains on the North Carolina–Tennessee border; the most visited national park.

name: Guadalupe Mountains
about: Guadalupe Peak, the highest point in Texas, and the remains of an ancient reef.

name: Haleakalā
about: The vast summit crater of a dormant volcano on Maui, famous for its sunrises.

name: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes
about: Kīlauea and Mauna Loa, two of the world’s most active volcanoes.

name: Hot Springs
about: Historic Bathhouse Row and the natural thermal springs of the town of Hot Springs.

name: Indiana Dunes
about: Sand dunes, beaches and wetlands along the southern shore of Lake Michigan.

name: Isle Royale
about: A remote island in Lake Superior, known for its wolves and moose.

name: Joshua Tree
about: Where the Mojave and Colorado deserts meet, with Joshua trees and giant boulders.

name: Katmai
about: Brown bears catching salmon at Brooks Falls, and the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes.

name: Kenai Fjords
about: The Harding Icefield and the glaciers that flow from it into coastal fjords.

name: Kings Canyon
about: Giant sequoias, including the General Grant Tree, and one of the deepest canyons in the US.

name: Kobuk Valley
about: Arctic sand dunes and the migration route of the Western Arctic caribou herd.

name: Lake Clark
about: Volcanoes, lakes and coastal brown bears southwest of Anchorage.

name: Lassen Volcanic
about: All four types of volcano, plus boiling mudpots and steaming vents.

name: Mammoth Cave
about: The longest known cave system in the world.

name: Mesa Verde
about: Cliff dwellings built by the Ancestral Puebloans, including Cliff Palace.

name: Mount Rainier
about: An active, glacier-covered volcano ringed by wildflower meadows.

name: New River Gorge
about: A deep river gorge known for whitewater rafting, climbing and its high bridge.

name: North Cascades
about: Jagged peaks with more than 300 glaciers in northern Washington.

name: Olympic
about: Temperate rainforest, glaciated mountains and wild Pacific coastline in one park.

name: Petrified Forest
about: Fossilized logs and the colourful badlands of the Painted Desert.

name: Pinnacles
about: Rock spires and talus caves, and a release site for the endangered California condor.

name: Redwood
about: Coast redwoods, the tallest trees on Earth, along the northern California coast.

name: Rocky Mountain
about: High peaks crossed by Trail Ridge Road, the highest continuous paved road in the US.

name: Saguaro
about: Forests of giant saguaro cacti on both sides of Tucson.

name: Sequoia
about: The General Sherman Tree, the largest tree on Earth by volume.

name: Shenandoah
about: The Blue Ridge Mountains and Skyline Drive.

name: Theodore Roosevelt
about: The North Dakota badlands where Theodore Roosevelt ranched, with bison and wild horses.

name: Virgin Islands
about: Beaches, coral reefs and trails covering much of the island of St. John.

name: Voyageurs
about: Lakes and islands on the Canadian border, best explored by boat.

name: White Sands
about: The world’s largest gypsum dunefield.

name: Wind Cave
about: One of the longest caves in the world, known for its boxwork, beneath a prairie.

name: Wrangell–St. Elias
about: The largest national park in the US, at more than 13 million acres.

name: Yellowstone
about: The world’s first national park, with Old Faithful and more than half the world’s geysers.

name: Yosemite
about: Granite cliffs such as El Capitan and Half Dome, waterfalls and giant sequoias.

name: Zion
about: Towering sandstone cliffs and hikes such as Angels Landing and The Narrows.
